primary.reasoning: tier_cliff: TE tier 3 has exactly two players left (Tyler Warren 116.8, Tucker Kraft 116.3) with a 10.6-point gap to tier 4, and tierCliffs flags TE atRisk=1. opponent_demand: Every one of the eight teams picking in the 16 selections before 69 lists TE as a need (teams 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 - TE:high for 2,3,4,5,6,8), so both remaining tier-3 TEs will almost certainly be gone; Juancho gives Warren only 10.5% survival and Kraft 28.7%. starter_need: TE is a mandatory starting slot we have not filled and a second TE is not a realistic FLEX in standard scoring, so this is a one-slot, one-chance position. survives_to_next_turn: The WR tier we would otherwise take from has 7 players left (Flowers, Jameson Williams, DeVonta Smith, Egbuka, McLaurin, Evans, Watson) and only teams 2,3,4,7,8 need WR, so a tier-8 WR should reach pick 69. first_seed_prior: Warren is fsRank 60 versus best available 52, an 8-rank reach - just inside the tolerance band - and Juancho's raw simulation actually prefers him (dPlan +12.5, the largest positive on the board); the -23.6 dDec is the anchor's reach penalty, which we are overruling on scarcity grounds. opportunity_cost: Passing Flowers costs roughly 1-3 projected points versus Jameson Williams/DeVonta Smith at 69, while passing Warren costs 10.6 points versus TE tier 4 (LaPorta 105.5, Andrews 105.7, Kittle 103.4).

alternatives.reasoning: Zay Flowers is First Seed's best available and would upgrade our second FLEX, but he is one of seven left in WR tier 8 with DeVonta Smith, Jameson Williams, Egbuka, McLaurin and Mike Evans behind him, so that tier survives to 69/72.
Joe Burrow is the top QB left in a three-deep tier 3 with a 12.9-point cliff after it, but in a 1QB league the gap to Herbert/Caleb Williams/Dak at pick 89+ is small enough to wait.

advice.roomRead: Roster 6: TE:high with QB and WRs already set and picks at 55 and 66 - the single most likely team to take Tyler Warren or Tucker Kraft before us. Roster 8: WR:high and TE:high, QB already filled with Drake Maye, picks at 53 and 68 - can take both a tier-8 WR and the last tier-3 TE. Roster 7: Already rostered Colston Loveland but still TE:medium and WR:high with picks at 54 and 67; more likely to take a WR from the tier we are passing on, which is why that tier thins but does not empty. Roster 2: WR:high and TE:high with four RBs already, picks at 59 and 62 - a direct competitor for both Warren and the tier-8 WRs. Roster 4: WR:critical and TE:high with five RBs, picks at 57 and 64 - will consume WR tier 8 bodies, but that tier is deep enough to absorb it. Roster 1: Has Trey McBride so TE is only medium; picks at 60 and 61 and needs QB, which slightly raises the chance a tier-3 QB like Burrow goes before 69.
advice.strategy: We are a balanced/RB-heavy build with all four RB/WR starting slots plus one FLEX already filled by Nacua, Pickens, Barkley, Javonte and Judkins; this pick deliberately breaks the RB/WR pattern to grab the last member of the separating TE tier before eight teams that all list TE as a need pick sixteen times.
advice.firstSeedDeviationReason: Reaching 8 ranks past First Seed's best available (Flowers, fsRank 52) to secure the last of two players in the TE tier-3 cliff; the WR tier behind Flowers is seven deep and refills at our next two picks, while every intervening team needs a TE, making this our only realistic shot at a 116-point starting tight end instead of a ~104-point one.
advice.expectedNextPickPlan: At 69 and 72 (back-to-back turn) we take one of the surviving tier-8 WRs (Jameson Williams, DeVonta Smith, Egbuka, McLaurin or Mike Evans) for the second FLEX and pair it with a QB from the tier-4 block - Herbert, Caleb Williams, Dak or Trevor Lawrence, all projected 282-287 and 16 deep, meaning one is certain to be there; 89/92 then go to RB depth (Croskey-Merritt, Jordan Mason) and the final rounds to K and DEF.
